# The container-sink matrix — see self_host_container_sink_matrix_test.go.
#
#   <cell> <native> <selfhost> <note>
#
# CONTAINER POSITION x what the source local does after the store. A store at
# the source's LAST USE is a move and has always worked; a source that stays
# LIVE (or is REBOUND) makes the store a counted SHARE, which needs the store's
# retain, an "APOWNED:" stamp from the pass that granted the container its
# element walk, and an rc-gated release on both owners.
#
# BOTH columns are clean on every cell, and that is the point of the file now:
# it is a regression gate, not a to-do list. It was not always — it opened with
# eight positions leaking, each retired by its own slice, and the shape those
# slices converged on is what a new cell should be read against:
#
#   - the construction RETAINS a bare-ident element (skipped at a MOVE site,
#     where the container takes over the source's reference instead);
#   - an "APOWNED:" stamp from the pass that granted the container its element
#     walk says which sites the container owns;
#   - the container's credit admits the counted element;
#   - BOTH releases are rc-gated, the source's via "SINKSHARE:". Half of that
#     pairing is not half a fix: with one owner gated and the other walking
#     statically, whichever sweep runs first frees the buffers and the other
#     frees them again. It shows up as exit 99 and NOT in the census, which
#     reads allocs == frees at live_bytes 0.
#
# A `leak` appearing here again means a position's release protocol regressed to
# refusing the source's credit rather than dangling. Exit codes must match
# between the compilers on every cell, and the underflow guard fails hard on
# either side: an over-release is a bug in any cell, listed or not.

arrlit__moved         clean clean  the literal admits a bare ident, stamped like a self-append
arrlit__live          clean clean  counted element: [p] retains, both owners release rc-gated
arrlit__rebound       clean clean
append__moved         clean clean
append__live          clean clean
append__rebound       clean clean  the stamp says who OWNS the element; the move analysis says who pays
append__blockscoped   clean clean  a retired source: the site key cannot fall through the way a slot predicate did

with__live            clean clean  a counted element, and the SUPERSEDED one is released at the store
with__moved           clean clean  `with` is a sanctioned self-store rebind now, so the container earns its walk
tuple__moved          clean clean  a MOVED struct element: the tuple is sole owner, so its walk is the one release
tuple__live           clean clean  the literal retains a struct element, so both owners release under the rc gate
variant__moved        clean clean  a MOVED struct payload: the enum's rc-gated payload drop is the one release
variant__live         clean clean  the ctor retains a struct payload, so both owners release under the rc gate
variant_unqual__moved clean clean  the bare spelling must measure identically — it used not to
variant_unqual__live  clean clean  and the bare spelling measures identically — the rc plan modelled only one of them
option__moved         clean clean  the match EXPRESSION is an inlined IIFE, so consuming_match_of sees the match through it
option__live          clean clean  and the store's own axis was already counted — see option_stmt
option_stmt__moved    clean clean  opt_make retains the struct box, so the option co-owns it and both releases are rc-gated
option_stmt__live     clean clean  a counted payload: the source stays live and each owner releases once
result_stmt__moved    clean clean  `Ok(p)` is the same box through the same lowering — it must measure identically
result_stmt__live     clean clean
